Of the Son, in Psalm 112 (verse 4):

> The Lord is Most High above all nations, and his glory is above the heavens.

Of the Holy Spirit, in Isaiah:

> Thus says the Most High, who dwells in the heights forever, the Holy One among the holy ones; the Lord Most High is his name, dwelling among the holy ones (Isa. 57:15).

## CHAPTER XVII. That the whole Trinity is called “Fire”

The Father is fire, the Son is fire, and the Holy Spirit is fire.

Of the Father, in Deuteronomy:

> Beware lest you make for yourselves any image or likeness of all the things concerning which God commanded you, because the Lord your God is a consuming fire (Deut. 4:23).

Of the Son, in Psalm 118 (verse 146):

> Your word is exceedingly fiery, and your servant has loved it.

Of the Holy Spirit, in the Acts of the Apostles:

> Tongues as though of fire appeared to them, divided among them, and one rested upon each of them; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:3).

## CHAPTER XVIII. That the whole Trinity is called “Light”

The Father is light, the Son is light, and the Holy Spirit is light.

Of the Father, in the Epistle of John:

> God is light, and there is no darkness in him at all (1 John 1:5).

Of the Son, in the Gospel:

> I am the light of this world; whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life (John 8:12).

Of the Holy Spirit, in Ezekiel:

> Behold, the Spirit of the Lord, rising, came from the north, and around him was resplendent light (Ezek. 1:4).

## CHAPTER XIX. On the common goodness of the Trinity

The Father is good, the Son is good, and the Holy Spirit is good.

Of the Father, in Psalm 72 (verse 1):

> How good is God to Israel, to those who are upright in heart.

Of the Son:

> I am the good shepherd (John 10:11).

And:

> Good Teacher, what good shall I do to have eternal life (Matt. 19:16)?

Of the Holy Spirit, in Ezra:

> You gave them your good Spirit (2 Esd. 9:20).

And in Solomon:

> Your good Spirit is in all things (Wis. 12:1).

## CHAPTER XX. On the common greatness of the Trinity

The Father is great, the Son is great, and the Holy Spirit is great.

Of the Father, in Exodus:

> Now I understand that God is great (Exod. 18:11).

And in Psalm 85 (verse 10):

> You alone are the great God.

Of the Son, in the Epistle to Titus:

> Awaiting the blessed hope and the coming of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ (Tit. 2:13).

Of the Holy Spirit, in the Books of Kings, the Lord says to Elijah:

> Go out and stand on the mountain before me. And behold, the Lord passes by, and a great and mighty spirit, overturning and shattering the rock before the Lord (1 Kings 19:11).

## CHAPTER XXI. On the common power of the Trinity

The Father is power, the Son is power, and the Holy Spirit is power.

Of the Father, the Apostle says to the Romans:

> I am not ashamed of the Gospel, for it is power unto salvation for everyone who believes (Rom. 1:16).

Of the Son, to the Corinthians:

> Therefore I will most gladly boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me (2 Cor. 12:9).

And of the Holy Spirit, to the Thessalonians:

> Knowing, brothers chosen by God, your love, because our Gospel did not come to you in word alone but in the power of the Holy Spirit (1 Thess. 1:4).

## CHAPTER XXII. Where the whole Trinity is called “Fountain”

The Father is fountain, the Son is fountain, and the Holy Spirit is fountain.

Of the Father, in Jeremiah:

> Thus says the Lord God of Israel: My people have committed two evils: they have abandoned me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water (Jer. 2:13).

Of the Son, in Solomon:

> The fountain of wisdom is the word of God in the heights (Sir. 1:5).

Of the Holy Spirit, in Isaiah:

> Behold, the name of God comes after a long time; burning in the wrath of indignation, he has devoured the nations, and the Spirit, like a fountain of water, draws through the valley (Isa. 30:27).

## CHAPTER XXIII. Where the whole Trinity is called “River”

[Col. 0417A]

The Father is river, the Son is river, and the Holy Spirit is river.

Of the Father, in Solomon:

> The blessing of God, like an overflowing river (Sir. 39:27);

and in Psalm 64 (verse 10):

> The river of God is filled with water.

Of the Son, in Isaiah:

> Thus says the Lord: I will incline toward them like a river of peace, and like an overflowing torrent, the glory of the nations (Isa. 66:12).

Again there:

> He will appear in Zion like a flowing river, bright in a thirsty land (Isa. 59:20).

Of the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel:

> On the great day of the feast Jesus stood and cried out, saying: “Whoever believes in me, as Scripture says, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.” Now he said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were to receive (John 7:37).

## CHAPTER XXIV. Where the Holy Spirit is called the Word, as is the Son

The Son is the Word of God the Father; the Holy Spirit is the Word of God.

Of the Son, in the Gospel:

> In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God (John 1:1).

And in the Apocalypse:

> He was clothed in a garment spattered with blood, and his name is called the Word of God (Rev. 19:13).

Of the Holy Spirit, in the Epistle to the Ephesians:

> In all things take up the shield of faith, with which you may extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one, and the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God (Eph. 6:16).

## CHAPTER XXV. That the whole Trinity is called “Love”

The Father is love, the Son is love, and the Holy Spirit is love.

Of the Father, in the Epistle of John:

> Little children, God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him (1 John 4:16).

Of the Son, to the Corinthians:

> Whether we have been carried beyond ourselves, it is for God; whether we are sober-minded, it is for you; for the love of Christ compels us (2 Cor. 5:13).

Of the Holy Spirit, to the Romans:

> I appeal to you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Holy Spirit (Rom. 15:30).

And to the Galatians:

> You were called to freedom (Gal. 5:13).

And below:

> But through the love of the Spirit serve one another.

And to the Corinthians he says:

> Do you wish me to come to you with a rod, or in the love of the Spirit (1 Cor. 4:21)?

## CHAPTER XXVI. That the whole Trinity bestows eternal life

The Father gives eternal life; the Son gives it; the Holy Spirit gives it.

Of the Father, in the Epistle of John:

> Whoever does not believe God makes him a liar, because he does not believe the testimony that he has testified concerning his Son. And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life (1 John 5:10).

Of the Son, in the Gospel:

> My sheep hear my voice and follow me, and I give them eternal life (John 10:27).

And in the Epistle of John:

> Whoever has the Son has eternal life (1 John 5:12).

Of the Holy Spirit, to the Galatians:

> Whoever sows in his flesh will reap corruption from the flesh; but whoever sows in the spirit will reap eternal life from the spirit (Gal. 6:8).

## CHAPTER XXVII. That the whole Trinity grants peace

The Father gives peace, the Son gives peace, and the Holy Spirit gives peace.

Again there:

> Our God, give us peace (Gal. 1:3).

And the Apostle:

> May the God of peace give you peace (2 Thess. 3:16).

And again:

> May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace, so that you may abound and glorify the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom. 15:13).

Of the Son, in Numbers:

> Thus says the Lord, who made Israel: Behold, I give them a covenant of peace, and you shall be with him and with his offspring after him (Num. 25:13).

Of the Holy Spirit, the Apostle says:

> The prudence of the flesh is death, but the prudence of the Spirit is life and peace (Rom. 8:6).

## CHAPTER XXVIII. On the common consolation

The Father consoles, the Son consoles, and the Holy Spirit consoles.

Of the Father, to the Corinthians:

> Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all consolation, who consoles us (2 Cor. 1:3).

Of the Son, in the passage cited above:

> For just as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so through Christ our consolation also abounds (ibid., 5).

Of the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel:

> When the Consoler comes, whom I shall send to you—the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from my Father—he will teach you all truth and announce to you the things that are to come (John 15:26).

## CHAPTER XXIX. On the common assistance of the Trinity

The Father helps, the Son helps, and the Holy Spirit helps.

Of the Father, in Psalm 45 (verse 6):

> God is in her midst; she will not be shaken. God will help her with his countenance.

Of the Son, in the Gospel:

> When Jesus came into the region of Tyre and Sidon, behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders, crying out and saying: “Help me, Lord” (Matt. 15:25).

Of the Holy Spirit, the Apostle says:

> For we do not know how to pray as we ought, but the Spirit himself helps our weakness (Rom. 8:26).

## CHAPTER XXX. On the common glory of the Trinity

The Father is the God of glory; so is the Son; so is the Holy Spirit.

Of the Father, in the Acts of the Apostles:

> The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia (Acts 7:2).

Of the Son, the Apostle says:

> For if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory (1 Cor. 2:8).

Of the Holy Spirit, to the Corinthians:

> Do you not know that your bodies are the temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God (1 Cor. 6:19)?

And below:

> Glorify and bear the Lord in your body (ibid., 20).

## CHAPTER XXXI. On the common teaching

The Father’s teaching, the Son’s teaching, and the Holy Spirit’s teaching.

Of the Father, in the Acts of the Apostles:

> When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, astonished at the teaching of God (Acts 13:12).

Of the Son, to Titus:

> Slaves are to be obedient to their masters in everything (Tit. 2:9).

And below:

> So that the teaching of our Savior Jesus Christ may be adorned in everything (Tit. 2:10).

And again:

> Whoever does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God (2 John 9).

Of the Holy Spirit, to the Corinthians:

> What we speak is not in words taught by human wisdom, but in the teaching of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor. 2:13).

## CHAPTER XXXII. On the common sanctification
The Father sanctifies, the Son sanctifies, the Holy Spirit sanctifies. Concerning the Father, to the Thessalonians: “We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by God, because he chose us from the beginning for salvation, in sanctification” (II Thess. II, 12). And the prophet: “God prepared a sacrifice and sanctified his chosen ones” (Zeph. I, 7). Concerning the Son, in the Apostle: “And such were some of you; but you were washed, and you were sanctified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ” [Col. 0419B] (I Cor. VI, 11). Concerning the Holy Spirit, 461 in the Catholic Epistles: “According to the providence of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit” (I Pet. I, 2). And to the Romans: “So that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit” (Rom. XV, 16).

### CHAPTER XXXIII. Concerning the common revelation.

The Father reveals, the Son reveals, the Holy Spirit reveals. Concerning the Father, to the Galatians: “But when it pleased God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb by his grace, to reveal his Son in me” (Gal. I, 15). Concerning the Son, to the Galatians: “For I did not receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ” (ibid., 12). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Ephesians: “What in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, but has now been revealed through the Holy Spirit to his holy apostles and prophets” [Col. 0419C] (Eph. III, 5).

### CHAPTER XXXIV. Concerning the common blessing.

The Father will bless you, the Son will bless you, the Holy Spirit will bless you. Concerning the Father, to the Ephesians: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing” (Eph. I, 3). Concerning the Son, in Solomon: “The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous” (Prov. X, 6). And in the eighty-third Psalm (verse 8): “He who gave the law will give a blessing.” Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Galatians: “So that the blessing of Abraham might come upon the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that we might receive the blessing of the Spirit” (Gal. III, 14).

### CHAPTER XXXV. Concerning the common joy of the Trinity. [Col. 0419D]

The Father gives joy, likewise the Son, likewise the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I give them everlasting joy, and I will cleanse them, and their works will be acceptable before me” (Isa. XXXV, 10). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “I will see you, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you” 462 (John XVI, 22). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Thessalonians: “You received the word amid great affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit” (I Thess. I, 6). And to the Romans: “For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit” (Rom. XIV, 17).

### CHAPTER XXXVI. Concerning the common regeneration.

[Col. 0420A]

The Father regenerates, the Son regenerates, the Holy Spirit regenerates. Concerning the Father, the Apostle says: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy regenerated us unto the hope of eternal life” (I Pet. I, 3). Concerning the Son, in the passage cited above: “In the love of the brethren, love one another, as those reborn through the word of the living God, which abides forever” (ibid., 22–23). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “Unless someone is born again of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God” (John III, 5).

### CHAPTER XXXVII. Concerning the common rest.

The Father gives rest, the Son gives rest, the Holy [Col. 0420B] Spirit gives rest. Concerning the Father, in Exodus: “The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: ‘Behold, you will be gathered to your fathers, and I will give you rest; and you will know that I am the Lord, who preserved you on your way’” (Exod. XXXIII, 14). Concerning the Son, to the Thessalonians: “So that you may be considered worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer” (II Thess. I, 5). And below: “Repay those who afflict you with affliction, and you who are afflicted with rest” (ibid., 6). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Apocalypse: “From now on,” says the Spirit, “let them rest from their labors” (Apoc. XIV, 13).

### CHAPTER XXXVIII. Concerning the common salvation.

The Father saves, the Son saves, the Holy Spirit saves. Concerning the Father, in the hundred-fifth Psalm (verse 47): [Col. 0420C] “Save us, O our God, and gather us from among the nations.” 463 Concerning the Son, in the hundred-first Psalm (verse 17): “For the Lord will save Zion, and he will appear in his majesty.” And in the Apostle: “For we have placed our hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all, especially of believers” (I Tim. IV, 10). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to Titus: “But when the kindness and humanity of our Savior God appeared, he saved us through the power of the regeneration of the Holy Spirit” (Titus III, 4).

### CHAPTER XXXIX. Concerning the common love.

The Father’s love, the Son’s love, the Holy Spirit’s love. Concerning the Father, the Apostle John says: “God is love” (I John IV, 16). And again: “If God loved us, we also ought to love one another” (ibid., 11). Concerning the Son, [Col. 0420D] in the Gospel: “As the Father loved me, so I loved you” (John XV, 9). And again: “Having loved his disciples, he loved them to the end” (John XIII, 1). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in John’s Epistle: “And by this we know that his love remains in us: by the Holy Spirit, whom he gave us” (I John IV, 1).

### CHAPTER XL. Concerning the common uprightness.

The Father is upright, the Son is upright, the Holy Spirit is upright. Concerning the Father, in the ninety-first Psalm (verse 16): “For the Lord our God is upright, and there is no injustice in him.” Concerning the Son, in the thirty-second Psalm (verse 4): “For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his works are in faithfulness.” Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the [Col. 0421A] fiftieth Psalm (verse 12): “Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.”

### CHAPTER XLI. Where the blessing of the Trinity is named.

Blessed is the Father, blessed is the Son, blessed is the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in the Gospel: “Blessed is the Lord, 464 the God of Israel, because he has visited and wrought redemption for his people” (Luke I, 78). Concerning the Son, to the Romans: “From them is Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all, blessed forever” (Rom. IX, 5). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Solomon: “Blessed is the spirit of the righteous from the Lord, and they will glory in his regard” (Ecclus. XXXIV, 14).

### CHAPTER XLII. Concerning the common strengthening. [Col. 0421B]

The Father strengthens, so does the Son, so does the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in Esther: “Strengthen me, O King of the gods, who hold all authority” (Esth. XIV, 12). Concerning the Son, the Apostle says: “I give thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, who strengthened me and judged me faithful, appointing me to the ministry” (I Tim. I, 12). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “But the child grew and was strengthened in spirit” (Luke I, 80).

### CHAPTER XLIII. Concerning the common resurrection.

The Father raises up, the Son raises up, the Holy Spirit raises up. Concerning the Father, in Acts: “The God of our fathers raised Jesus, and he will raise us up by his power” (Acts II, 32). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: [Col. 0421C] “Many of the Jews had come there, not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead” (John XII, 9). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Apostle: “But if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he will give life to your mortal bodies through his Holy Spirit dwelling in you” (Rom. VIII, 11).

### CHAPTER XLIV. Concerning the common invisibility.

The Father is invisible, the Son is invisible, so is the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, to the Colossians: “Who is the image of the invisible God” (Col. I, 15). Concerning the Son, in the Book of Job: “Where will you find the wisdom of God? For it is hidden from the sight of all, and concealed from the birds of heaven” [Col. 0421D] (Job XXVIII, 21). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the passage cited above: “And a spirit passed before my face, and the hairs of my flesh bristled, and I saw neither flesh nor face nor form, but I heard only a voice” (Job IV, 15).

### CHAPTER XLV. Concerning the common giving of life.

The Father gives life, the Son gives life, so does the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, to the Romans: “I have appointed you the father of many nations before God, in whom you believed, who gives life” (Rom. IV, 17). Concerning the Son, in Kings: “The Lord puts to death and gives life” (I Kings II, 6). And in the Gospel: “As the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wills” (John V, 21). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Epistle of the Apostle Peter: “Put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the spirit” [Col. 0422A] (I Pet. III, 18). And the Apostle Paul: “The letter kills, but the spirit gives life” (II Cor. III, 6).

### CHAPTER XLVI. Where the Trinity is called the grace of God.

The grace of God the Father, the grace of the Son, the grace of the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, to the Romans: “Much more has the grace of God, and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus Christ, abounded for the many” (Rom. V, 15). Likewise there: “Who will deliver me from this body of death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ” (Rom. VII, 24). Concerning the Son, to the Corinthians: “For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: although he was rich, he became poor for your sake” (II Cor. VIII, 9). Concerning the Spirit, in Acts: “The Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard the word, [Col. 0422B] and the faithful from the circumcision who had come with Peter were amazed, because the grace of the Holy Spirit had also been poured out upon the Gentiles” (Acts X, 44).

### CHAPTER XLVII. Concerning the common renewal.

The Father renews, the Son renews, so does the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in Jeremiah: “Convert us, O God, and we shall be converted to you; renew our days as at the beginning” 466 (Lam. V, 21). Concerning the Son, in Solomon: “But she reaches mightily from end to end and orders all things sweetly” (Wis. VIII, 1), and, “Though she is one, she renews all things” (Wis. VII, 17). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Romans: “But now we have been released from the law of death in which we were held, so that we may serve in the newness of the spirit and not in the oldness of the letter” (Rom. VII, 6).

### CHAPTER XLVIII. Concerning the common seal of the Trinity. [Col. 0422C]

The Father seals, the Son seals, the Holy Spirit seals. Concerning the Father, to the Corinthians: “But he who confirms us with you in Christ, and Christ in you, and who anointed us—God—and sealed us” (II Cor. I, 21). Concerning the Son, to the Ephesians: “When you heard the word of the Gospel of your salvation, in which you believed, you were sealed” (Eph. I, 13). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the passage cited above: “Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption” (Eph. IV, 30).

### CHAPTER XLIX. Concerning the common anointing.

The Father anoints, the Son anoints, the Holy Spirit anoints. Concerning the Father, in the forty-fourth Psalm (verse 8): [Col. 0422D] “Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness.” And in the eighty-eighth Psalm (verse 21): “I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.” Concerning the Son, in John’s Epistle: “And the anointing that we received from the Holy One remains in us, and you have no need for anyone to teach you” (I John II, 27). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Isaiah: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor” (Isa. LXI, 1).

### CHAPTER L. Concerning the common reproving.

The Father reproves, the Son reproves, the Holy Spirit reproves. Concerning the Father, in Solomon: “Do not say, ‘Our God is merciful; he will not repay us for our sins’; for in his patience he will finally reprove sinners” 467 [Col. 0423A] (Ecclus. V, 6–7). Concerning the Son, in Isaiah: “For the law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem; and he will judge among the nations and reprove many peoples” (Isa. II, 3–4). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “When that Holy Spirit comes, whom the Father will send in my name, he will reprove the world concerning sin” (John XVI, 8).

### CHAPTER LI. Concerning the common gathering.

The Father gathers, the Son gathers, the Holy Spirit gathers. Concerning the Father, in the hundred-fifth Psalm (verse 47): “Save us, O our God, and gather us from among the nations.” Concerning the Son, in Isaiah: “And those redeemed by the Lord will walk there, gathered together” (Isa. XXXV, 9). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Isaiah: “For the Lord commanded them, and his Spirit gathered them” [Col. 0423B] (Isa. XXXIV, 16).

### CHAPTER LII. That the whole Trinity is present everywhere.

The Father is everywhere, the Son is everywhere, the Holy Spirit is everywhere. Concerning the Father, in Jeremiah: “Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I fill heaven and earth” (Jer. XXIII, 24). Likewise in Isaiah: “Heaven is my throne, but the earth is the footstool of my feet” (Isa. LXVI, 1). Concerning the Son, in Solomon: “But wickedness will not overcome wisdom” (Wis. VII, 30). “She reaches mightily from end to end” (Wis. VIII, 1). And in the hundred-second Psalm (verse 22): “In every place of his dominion.” Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Psalm: “Where shall I go from your Spirit, [Col. 0423C] and where shall I flee from your presence? If I descend into the abyss, you are there” (Ps. CXXXVIII, 7), etc.

### CHAPTER LIII. Concerning the common deliverance.

The Father delivers, the Son delivers, the Holy Spirit delivers. Concerning the Father, in the seventy-seventh Psalm (verse 35): “And they remembered that God was their helper, and that God Most High was their deliverer.” And in the fifty-sixth Psalm (verses 3–4): “I will cry to God Most High, to the Lord who has done good to me; he sent from heaven and delivered me,” etc. Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “If the Son sets you free, you will truly be free; and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free” (John VIII, 36, 32). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Apostle: “The Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has delivered me from the law of sin [Col. 0423D] and death” (Rom. VIII, 2). And: “Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom” (II Cor. III, 17).

### CHAPTER LIV. Concerning the common rebuking.

The Father rebukes, the Son rebukes, the Holy Spirit rebukes. Concerning the Father, in the hundred-fifth Psalm (verses 8–9): “To make his power known, he rebuked the Red Sea, and it was dried up.” Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “And rising, he rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm” (Luke VIII, 24). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the song of Exodus: “And by the spirit of your anger the water was divided; the waves froze in the midst of the sea” (Exod. XV, 8).

### CHAPTER LV. Where the Son and the Holy Spirit have received the name of Advocate.

[Col. 0424A]

The Son is Advocate, the Holy Spirit is Advocate. Concerning the Son, in the Epistle of the Apostle John: “Little children, do not sin. But if we sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous” (I John II, 1). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, an Advocate, the Spirit of truth” (John XIV, 16).

### CHAPTER LVI. Where the Son and the Holy Spirit alike intercede for the faithful.

The Son intercedes, the Holy Spirit intercedes. Concerning the Son, to the Romans: “Who will bring an accusation against God’s elect? God, who justifies. Who is he who condemns? [Col. 0424B] Christ Jesus, who died, but rather was also raised, who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us” (Rom. VIII, 33). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the passage cited above: “But if we hope for what we do not see, we await it with patience. Likewise the Spirit also intercedes for our weakness” (verses 25–26).

### CHAPTER LVII. Concerning the common building up.

The Father builds up, the Son builds up, the Holy Spirit builds up. Concerning the Father, to the Corinthians: “We are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s building” (I Cor. III, 9). And again: “If I should boast somewhat more abundantly about our authority, which God gave us for building up the faithful” (II Cor. X, 8). Concerning the Son, in the hundred-forty-sixth [Col. 0424C] Psalm (verse 2): “The Lord builds up Jerusalem and gathers the dispersed of Israel.” Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Judith: “You are great and glorious and wonderful in power” (Judith XVI, 16). And below: “Let every creature serve you, because you spoke and they came to be; you sent your Spirit, and they were built up” (verse 17).

### CHAPTER LVIII. Where the Trinity grants chastity.

The Father gives chastity, the Son gives it, the Holy Spirit gives it. Concerning the Father, in Ezra: “You are the strong, great, mighty, and fearful God, who keeps the covenant and mercy” (Ezra I, 5). Concerning the Son, in the Apostle: “But I fear that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, so your minds may be corrupted from the chastity that is in Christ Jesus” (II Cor. XI, 3). Concerning the Holy [Col. 0424D] Spirit, in the Epistle of the Apostle Peter: “Your souls, through the Spirit, by chastity, for obedience of faith” (I Pet. I, 22).

### CHAPTER LIX. Concerning the common indwelling.

The Father dwells in believers, the Son dwells in them, the Holy Spirit dwells in them. Concerning the Father, in Isaiah: “Thus says the Lord God Almighty: Observe the Sabbath day and sanctify it, so that I may dwell in your midst” (Isa. LVI, 4). Concerning the Son, in the Apocalypse: “Behold, the tabernacle of God is with human beings, and he will dwell with them on earth” (Apoc. XXI, 3). And again: “I will dwell in them, and walk among them, says the Lord” (II Cor. VI, 16). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Corinthians: “Do you not know that [Col. 0425A] you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?” (I Cor. III, 16).

### CHAPTER LX. Concerning the common knowledge.

The Father is known, the Son is known, the Holy Spirit is known. Concerning the Father, to the Galatians: “But now, knowing God—or rather, being known by God” (Gal. IV, 9). And in John’s Epistle: “I write to you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning” (I John II, 13). Concerning the Son and the Father, in the Gospel: “So that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent” (John XVII, 3). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Paraclete, the Spirit of truth” (John XIV, 16). And below: “But you know him, because he is with you” (ibid., 17).

### CHAPTER LXI. Concerning the common election. [Col. 0425B]

The Father chooses, the Son chooses, the Holy Spirit chooses. Concerning the Father, in the Apostle: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who chose us before the foundation of the world” (Eph. I, 3–4). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “You did not choose me, but I chose you from the world” (John XV, 16). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Acts: “When they had fasted and prayed, the Holy Spirit said to them: ‘Set apart for me Barnabas and Paul for the work to which I have chosen them’” (Acts XIII, 2).

### CHAPTER LXII. Concerning the common kingdom.

The Father reigns, the Son reigns, the Holy Spirit reigns. [Col. 0425C] Concerning the Father, in the Gospel: “Unless someone is born again of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot see the kingdom of God” (John III, 5). Concerning the Son, in the ninety-fifth Psalm (verse 10): “Say among the nations: ‘The Lord has reigned from the wood.’” Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Solomon: “By the Spirit of the Lord authority has been given to you” (Wis. VI, 4). And below: “And although you are ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged rightly” (ibid., 5).

### CHAPTER LXIII. Concerning the common searching.

The Father searches, the Son searches, the Holy Spirit searches. Concerning the Father, in the hundred-thirty-eighth Psalm (verse 23): “Prove me, O Lord, and know my heart; search me, and know my paths.” Concerning [Col. 0425D] the Son, in the Apocalypse: “And all the churches shall know that I am the one who searches heart and kidneys” (Apoc. II, 23). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Apostle: “For the Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God” (I Cor. II, 10).

### CHAPTER LXIV. Concerning the common testing.

The Father tests, the Son tests, the Holy Spirit tests. Concerning the Father, to the Thessalonians: “So we speak, not as pleasing human beings, but God, who tests our hearts” (I Thess. II, 4). Concerning the Son, in Solomon: “As gold in the furnace he tested them, and found them worthy of himself” (Wis. III, 6). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Solomon: “The Spirit of the Lord tests hearts” (Prov. XVII, 3); “but he will exterminate the wicked from the earth” (Prov. II, 22).

### CHAPTER LXV. Concerning the common testimony.

[Col. 0426A]

The Father bears witness, the Son bears witness, the Holy Spirit bears witness. Concerning the Father, in the eighteenth Psalm (verse 8): “The testimony of God is faithful, giving wisdom to the little ones.” Concerning the Son, to Timothy: “I charge you before God, who confirms all things, and Christ Jesus, who bore witness before Pontius Pilate” (I Tim. VI, 13). 472 Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Apostle: “For the Spirit himself bears witness to our spirit” (Rom. VIII, 16).

### CHAPTER LXVI. Concerning the common creation.

The Father is called Creator, and so are the Son and the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, to the Ephesians: “To enlighten all concerning the dispensation of the mystery hidden for ages in God, who created all things” [Col. 0426B] (Eph. III, 9). Concerning the Son, to the Romans: “They worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed God over all forever” (Rom. I, 25). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Solomon: “He saw, numbered, and measured all things; he himself created them through the Holy Spirit” (Ecclus. I, 9).

### CHAPTER LXVII. Concerning the common leadership.

The Father is called Leader, and so are the Son and the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in Deuteronomy: “And Moses said to the whole assembly of the children of Israel: ‘Know and understand that your God brought you out from the midst of the Egyptians with a strong hand and an outstretched arm’” (Deut. XXVI, 8). Concerning the Son, in Genesis: “The ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor the leader from his thighs, until he comes to whom it has been reserved, and in his name the nations shall hope” (Gen. XLIX, 10). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Ezekiel: “The Spirit of the Lord led me out and set me in the middle of a plain, and it was full of the bones of the dead” (Ezek. XXXVII, 3).

### CHAPTER LXVIII. Concerning the common calling.

The Father calls, the Son calls, the Holy Spirit calls. Concerning the Father, to the Corinthians: “Let each person walk as God has called him, as I also teach in all the churches” (I Cor. VII, 17). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “As Jesus was passing by, he saw a certain man sitting at the tax booth, named Matthew, and he called him, 473 and said to him: ‘Follow me’” (Matt. IX, 9). Concerning the Holy Spirit [Col. 0426D] in Acts: “While they were serving God, the Holy Spirit said to them: ‘Set apart for me Barnabas and Paul for the work to which I have called them’” (Acts XIII, 2).

### CHAPTER LXIX. Concerning the common mercy.

The Father is merciful, so is the Son, so is the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in the Apostle: “But God, who is rich in mercy, in his great love took pity on us” (Eph. II, 4). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “I have compassion on this crowd, because they have been with me for three days, and I do not want to send them away hungry” (Matt. XV, 32). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Zechariah: “Behold, I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a Spirit of grace and compassion” (Zech. XII, 10).

### CHAPTER LXX. Concerning the common indwelling of the temple.

[Col. 0427A]

The Father’s temple, the Son’s temple, the Holy Spirit’s temple. Concerning the Father, in the Apostle: “For the temple of God is holy, and you are that temple. Let no one deceive you: if anyone violates the temple of God, God will destroy him” (I Cor. III, 17). Concerning the Son, in the Apocalypse: “And the streets of the city were pure gold, and I saw no temple in it; for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple” (Apoc. XXI, 22). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Corinthians: “Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God?” (I Cor. VI, 19).

### CHAPTER LXXI. Concerning the common appointment.

The Father appoints, likewise the Son, likewise the Holy Spirit. [Col. 0427B] Concerning the Father, Jeremiah: “The Lord God said: ‘Behold, today I have appointed you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot and destroy, to rebuild and to plant’” (Jer. I, 10). Concerning the Son, in Acts: “On the day when he chose the apostles through the Holy Spirit, to whom he appointed them to preach 474 the Gospel” (Acts I, 2). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the passage cited above: “Pay attention to yourselves and to the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has appointed you bishops” (Acts XX, 28).

### CHAPTER LXXII. Concerning the common manifestation.

The Father manifests, the Son manifests, the Holy Spirit manifests. Concerning the Father, to the Romans: “Because what is known of God is manifest among them, for God manifested it to them” (Rom. I, 19). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “Jesus performed this first of his signs in Cana of Galilee, [Col. 0427C] and manifested his power” (John II, 11). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Corinthians: “To each person the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common benefit” (I Cor. XII, 7).

### CHAPTER LXXIII. Concerning the common showing.

The Father shows, the Son shows, the Holy Spirit shows. Concerning the Father, to Timothy: “Keep the commandment without stain and beyond reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ, whom the blessed and only powerful King of kings and Lord of lords will show at his proper times” (I Tim. VI, 14). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “I say to you, my friends, do not fear those who kill the body and after that have nothing more that they can do; but I will show you whom you should fear” (Luke XII, 4). And in the Gospel: “I have shown you many good works; for which of these works are you stoning me?” [Col. 0427D] (John X, 32). Concerning the Holy Spirit, to the Corinthians: “My speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in a showing of the Spirit and of power” (I Cor. II, 4).

### CHAPTER LXXIV. Concerning the common measure.

The Father gives measure, the Son gives measure, the Holy Spirit gives measure. Concerning the Father, to the Romans: “Not to think more highly than one ought to think, but to think with moderation, each according to the measure of faith that God has apportioned” (Rom. XII, 3). Concerning the Son, to the Corinthians: “But we ourselves, measuring and comparing ourselves among ourselves, do not boast beyond measure, [Col. 0428A] but according to the measure of the rule by which the Lord Jesus measured out to us the measure of reaching even to you” (II Cor. X, 12). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Solomon: “The spirit of wisdom fills with peace and gives the fruit of salvation; he saw, numbered, and measured both things in the gift of God” (Ecclus. I, 22).

### CHAPTER LXXV. Concerning the common modesty.

The Father’s modesty, the Son’s modesty, the Holy Spirit’s modesty. Concerning the Father, in Jeremiah: “O God, who in your holy modesty established all things, I beseech you to grant your servants favor in the sight of the king of Babylon, to whom you delivered us because of the sins of us and of our fathers” (Baruch II, 14). Concerning the Son, to the Corinthians: “I beseech you, brothers, by the gentleness and modesty of Christ” [Col. 0428B] (II Cor. X, 1). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Epistle of the Apostle Peter: “Not outwardly through braided hair, or the wearing of gold, or an elegant style of clothing, but the hidden person in the incorruptible modesty of the Spirit, which is precious before God” (I Pet. III, 3).

### CHAPTER LXXVI. Concerning the common sending.

The Father sent, the Son sent, the Holy Spirit sent. Concerning the Father, in the Apostle: “God sent his Son in the likeness of sinful flesh” (Rom. VIII, 3). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “I sent you to reap where you did not sow” (John IV, 38). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Acts: “While Peter was hesitating over the vision, the Holy Spirit said to him: ‘Arise, go with them, because I sent them’” (Acts X, 20).

### CHAPTER LXXVII. [Col. 0428C] Concerning the common protection.

476 The Father protects, the Son protects, the Holy Spirit protects. Concerning the Father, in the eighty-third Psalm (verse 10): “O Protector, now look upon the face of your anointed one.” Concerning the Son, in the sixteenth Psalm (verse 8): “Guard me, O Lord, as the apple of your eye; protect me under the shadow of your wings.” Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Solomon: “The Spirit of the Lord is protection and a bulwark of strength” (Ecclus. XXXIV, 19).

### CHAPTER LXXVIII. Concerning the common finger of the Trinity.

The Father’s finger, the Son’s finger, the Holy Spirit’s finger. Concerning the Father, in Exodus: “The magicians said to Pharaoh the king: ‘This is the finger of God’” (Exod. VIII, 19). Likewise there: “And Moses received the two tablets written by the finger of God” (Exod. XXXI, [Col. 0428D] 18). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “And Jesus, bending down, was writing on the ground with his finger” (John VIII, 6). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “But if I cast out demons by the finger of God, surely the kingdom of God has come upon you” (Luke XI, 20). In another place: “But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, know that the kingdom of God has come upon you” (Matt. XII, 28).

### CHAPTER LXXIX. Concerning the common faith.

The Father’s faith, the Son’s faith, the Holy Spirit’s faith. Concerning the Father, to the Romans: “For what if some of them did not believe? Will their unbelief nullify the faith of God?” (Rom. III, 3). Concerning the Son, in the Apostle: “But the life I now live in the flesh, I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved [Col. 0429A] me” (Gal. II, 20). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the passage cited above: “Having the same spirit of faith, as it is written: ‘I believed, therefore I spoke’” (II Cor. IV, 13).

### CHAPTER LXXX. Concerning the common prediction.

477 The Father foretold, the Son foretold, the Holy Spirit foretold. Concerning the Father, in Acts: “But God fulfilled what he had foretold through the mouth of all his holy prophets concerning his Christ” (Acts III, 18). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “And announce to the brothers that he is going before you into Galilee; there you will see him. Behold, I have foretold it to you” (Matt. XXVIII, 7). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Acts: “But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and said: ‘Men, brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who was [Col. 0429B] leader of those who seized Jesus’” (Acts I, 16).

### CHAPTER LXXXI. Concerning the common teaching.

The Father teaches, the Son teaches, the Holy Spirit teaches. Concerning the Father, in the seventieth Psalm (verse 17): “You have taught me, O God, from my youth.” And in the hundred-forty-third Psalm (verse 1): “Blessed be the Lord God, who teaches my hands for battle and my fingers for war.” Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “And Jesus went around all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues” (Matt. IV, 23). And again: “When he had sat down, he opened his mouth and taught them” (Matt. V, 2). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “But when that Paraclete, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will teach you all truth” (John XVI, 13).

### CHAPTER LXXXII. [Col. 0429C] Concerning the common command.

The Father commands, likewise the Son, likewise the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in the Second Epistle of Peter: “For if you do these things, you will never fall, but entry into the eternal kingdom of God will be supplied to you” (II Pet. I, 10). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “Deaf and mute spirit, I command you: come out of him, and do not enter him again” (Mark IX, 24). 478 And: “He commanded the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm” (Matt. VIII, 26). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Job (Job XXXVIII, 29): “From the Spirit of the Lord ice is given upon the earth.” And below: “By his command he made the snow; by his power he turned the heavens around the circuit of his glory” (Job XXXVII, 6).

### CHAPTER LXXXIII. [Col. 0429D] Concerning the common discipline.

The Father’s discipline, the Son’s discipline, the Holy Spirit’s discipline. Concerning the Father, in Solomon: “My son, do not neglect the discipline of God, nor grow faint when reproved by him” (Prov. III, 11). Concerning the Son, in the seventeenth Psalm (verse 36): “Your right hand received me, and your discipline itself will teach me, and your instruction will guide me to the end.” Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Solomon: “For the spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and will withdraw from thoughts that lack understanding” (Wis. I, 5).

### CHAPTER LXXXIV. Concerning the common breathing.

The Father breathes, the Son breathes, the Holy Spirit breathes. Concerning the Father, in Genesis: “And God made the human being in his image, and breathed into his face the breath of life, and the human being became a living soul” [Col. 0430A] (Gen. II, 7). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “And he breathed upon the faces of his disciples, saying: ‘Receive the Holy Spirit’” (John XX, 22). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Ezekiel: “Thus says the Lord: ‘Come from the four winds, O Spirit, and breathe upon these dead, and they shall live again’” (Ezek. XXXVII, 9).

### CHAPTER LXXXV. Concerning the common filling.

The Father fills, the Son fills, the Holy Spirit fills. Concerning the Father, in Jeremiah: “Thus says the Lord God of Israel: ‘I fill heaven and earth’” (Jer. XXIII, 24). Concerning the Son, in the Apostle: “But may the Lord fill your hearts with every good work and word” (II Tim. II, 16). [Col. 0430B] Concerning the Holy Spirit, 479, in Acts: “Suddenly there was a sound like that of a mighty spirit, and it filled the whole place where they were sitting” (Acts II, 2).

### CHAPTER LXXXVI. Concerning the common gift.

The gift of God the Father, the gift of the Son, and the gift of the Holy Spirit. Concerning the Father, in the Apostle: “By grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from you; it is the gift of God” (Eph. II, 8). Concerning the Son, in Solomon: “For no one can be continent unless God grants it; and this itself was wisdom, to know whose gift it was” (Wis. VIII, 21). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in Acts: “Repent, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit” (Acts II, 38).

### CHAPTER LXXXVII. [Col. 0430C] Concerning the common speech.

The Father speaks, the Son speaks, the Holy Spirit speaks. Concerning the Father, in the sixty-first Psalm (verse 12): “God has spoken once; I have heard these two things.” And: “God spoke in his holy place” (Ps. CVII, 8). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “As Jesus was speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak with him” (Matt. XII, 46). Likewise there: “I speak to you, and you do not believe” (John X, 25). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Apostle: “It is the Spirit who speaks mysteries” (I Cor. XIV, 2).

### CHAPTER LXXXVIII. Concerning the common recompense.

The Father will repay, the Son will repay, the Holy [Col. 0430D] Spirit will repay. Concerning the Father, in the Apostle: “Since it is indeed just before God to repay affliction to those who afflict you, and rest to you who are afflicted” (II Thess. I, 6). Concerning the Son, in the Apostle: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord” (Rom. XII, 19). Concerning the Holy Spirit, 480 in Judges: “For if they gather together and come to the borders of Jerusalem and attack you, I will send my Spirit, and he will repay them what they themselves repaid you.”

### CHAPTER LXXXIX. Concerning the common regard.

The Father regards, the Son regards, the Holy Spirit regards. Concerning the Father, in Genesis: “God looked upon Abel and his offerings; but upon Cain and his offerings he did not look” [Col. 0431A] (Gen. IV, 4). Concerning the Son, in the Gospel: “Jesus, seeing their thoughts, said: ‘Why are you thinking evil in your hearts?’” (Matt. IX, 4). Concerning the Holy Spirit, in the Apocalypse: “These are the seven spirits who look upon the whole earth” (Apoc. V, 6).

### CHAPTER XC. Concerning the common pleasure.

It pleased the Father, it pleased the Son, it pleased the Holy Spirit. Of the Father, in the Apostle: “After it pleased God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb, to reveal his Son in me” (Gal. 1:15). And in the Psalm: “It pleased God more than a young bull producing horns and hoofs” (Ps. 68:32). Of the Son, in Psalm 67 (v. 17): “The mountain on which it pleased God to dwell in it; for indeed the Lord will dwell [Col. 0431B] there forever,” etc. Of the Holy Spirit, in Acts: “It pleased the Holy Spirit and us to impose no further burden upon you” (Acts 15:28), etc.

## CHAPTER XCI. On the common understanding.

The Father gives understanding, the Son does so, and the Holy Spirit does so. Of the Father, in Psalm 15 (v. 7): “I will bless the Lord, who has granted me understanding.” Of the Son, in the Apostle: “Understand what I say, for the Lord will give you understanding” (2 Tim. 2:7). Of the Holy Spirit, in the passage cited above: “Therefore, from the day on which we heard, we have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding” (Col. 1:9).

## CHAPTER XCII. On the common cleansing. [Col. 0431C]

The Father cleanses, the Son cleanses, and the Holy Spirit cleanses. Of the Father, in Ezekiel: “He saves them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned; I will cleanse them, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God. My servant David shall be king over them, and he shall be shepherd of them all” (Ezek. 37:23). Of the Son, in the Gospel: “He has his winnowing shovel in his hand, and he will cleanse his threshing floor and gather his grain into his barns; but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire” (Matt. 3:12). And: “The flesh and blood of his Son cleanses us from every sin” (1 John 1:7). Of the Holy Spirit, in Isaiah: “And the Lord will cleanse the filth of the sons and daughters of Zion, and he will purge the blood of Jerusalem from her midst by the spirit of judgment and the spirit of burning” (Isa. 4:4). [Col. 0431D]

## CHAPTER XCIII. On the common illumination.

The Father illuminates, the Son illuminates, and the Holy Spirit illuminates. Of the Father, in Psalm 17 (v. 29): “You will illuminate my lamp; Lord my God, illuminate my darkness.” Of the Son, in the Apostle: “When the Lord comes, he will illuminate the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the thoughts of their hearts” (1 Cor. 4:5). And again: “Rise, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will illuminate you” (Eph. 5:19). Of the Holy Spirit, in the Apostle: “So that the illumination of the Holy Spirit may shine in them” (2 Cor. 4:4). [Col. 0432A]

## CHAPTER XCIV. On the common appearing.

The Father appeared, the Son appeared, and the Holy Spirit appeared. Of the Father, in Acts: “The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia” (Acts 7:2). Of the Son, in the Epistle of John: “The Son himself appeared in order to destroy the works of the devil” (1 John 3:8). Of the Holy Spirit, in Job: “And a spirit appeared before my eyes; and the hairs of my head bristled, and I did not see its face or form, but I heard only a voice” (Job 4:15). 482

## CHAPTER XCV. On the common truth.

The Father is truth, the Son is truth, and so also is the Holy Spirit. [Col. 0432B] Of the Father, in Psalm 30 (v. 6): “You have redeemed me, Lord, God of truth. Into your hands, Lord, I commend my spirit.” Of the Son, in the Gospel: “I am the way, the truth, and the life” (John 14:6). Likewise, he says to the Father: “Your word is truth” (John 17:17). Of the Holy Spirit, in the Epistle of John: “The Spirit is truth” (1 John 5:6).

## CHAPTER XCVI. On the common command.

The Father commands, the Son commands, and so also does the Holy Spirit. Of the Father, in Psalm 67 (v. 29): “Command, O God, your power.” And: “He commanded his covenant forever” (Ps. 110:9). Of the Son, in the Gospel: “I command you this: love one another” [Col. 0432C] (John 15:17). Of the Holy Spirit, in Isaiah: “Nevertheless, keep my ordinances, which I command you through my Spirit, says the Lord.”

## CHAPTER XCVII. On the common inspiration.

The Father inspires, the Son inspires, and the Holy Spirit inspires. Of the Father, in the Book of Job: “The spirit that made me, and the breath of the Almighty, teaches me” (Job 32:8). Of the Son, in Psalm 17 (v. 14): “At your rebuke, Lord, at the breath of the spirit of your wrath.” Of the Holy Spirit, in the Gospel: “The Spirit breathes where he wishes, and you hear his voice” (John 3:8), etc. 483

## CHAPTER XCVIII. On the common signification.

[Col. 0432D] The Father signifies, the Son signifies, and so also does the Holy Spirit. Of the Father, in Psalm 59 (v. 6): “O God, you have rejected us and led us.” And below: “You have given a sign to those who fear you, so that they may flee from before the bow.” Of the Son, in the Apocalypse: “The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show his servants, and he signified it, sending it through his angel to his servant John” (Rev. 1:1). Of the Holy Spirit, in the Epistle to the Hebrews: “Not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the ignorance of the people, the Holy Spirit signifying this” (Heb. 9:7).

## CHAPTER XCIX. On the common evangelization.

The Gospel of God the Father, the Gospel of the Son, and the Gospel of the Holy Spirit. Of the Father, in the Epistle to Timothy: “And if anything else is contrary to sound doctrine, which is according to the Gospel of the glory of the blessed God” (1 Tim. 1:10). Of the Son, in the Epistle to the Ephesians: “Destroying hostility in himself, and coming, he proclaimed peace” (Eph. 2:16). Likewise there: “For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the Gospel of his Son” (Rom. 1:9). Of the Holy Spirit, in the Epistle of Peter: “But these things were shown to you by those who proclaimed the Gospel to you in the Holy Spirit” (1 Pet. 1:12).

## CHAPTER C. Where the Trinity shone forth.

[Col. 0434A]

484 The Father shone forth, the Son shone forth, and the Holy Spirit shone forth. Of the Father, in the Apostle: “But the God who said, ‘Let light shine out of darkness,’ has shone in your hearts” (2 Cor. 4:6). Of the Son, in Psalm 117 (vv. 26–27): “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; the Lord is God, and he has shone upon us.” Of the Holy Spirit, in the prophet: “My face shall no longer be hidden from them, because my Spirit has shone upon the whole house of Israel, says the Lord” (Ezek. 39:29).

[Col. 0433B]

# THE TWO BOOKS OF VIGILIUS OF TAPSUS AGAINST PALLADIUS THE ARIAN (C, G, S)*

## BOOK ONE: THE RECORD OF THE BISHOPS OF AQUILEIA AGAINST THE ARIAN HERETICS

[Col. 0433]

[Col. 0433B] 485 In the consulship of the most distinguished men Syagrius and Eucherius, on the third day before the Nones of September, while the bishops were seated at Aquileia in the church—the bishops of the city of Aquileia, Valerian, Ambrose, Eusebius, Limenius, Anemius, Sabinus, Abundantius, Artemius, Constantius, Justus, Philaster, Constantius, Theodore, Almachius, Domninus, Amantius, Maximus, Felix, Bassianus, Numidius, Januarius, Proculus, Heliodorus, Jovinus, Felix, Exsuperantius, Diogenes, Maximus, Macedonius, Cassianus, Marcellus, and Eustathius.

Bishop Ambrose said: “For a long time we have conducted our proceedings outside the official record. And since such great sacrileges are being thrust upon our ears by Palladius and Secundianus that scarcely anyone could believe they were capable of blaspheming so openly—and lest they later attempt by some trick to deny what they have said, although the testimony of so many priests cannot be doubted—nevertheless, since all the bishops approve, let an official record be made, so that no one may later be able to deny his own profession. What, then, you holy men approve must be declared.”

All the bishops said: “We approve.”

486 Bishop Ambrose said: “Our discussions must be confirmed in writing by the imperial document, so that it may be introduced as evidence.”

The deacon Sabinianus read:

“Because of the ambiguous reverence surrounding doctrines, lest the priests disagree, and because we wished to test the matter as soon as possible, we had ordered the bishops to assemble in the city of Aquileia, entrusted by reason of its merits to your distinguished authority. For doubtful controversies could not be settled more suitably than by appointing the bishops themselves as interpreters of the dispute that had arisen, so that the disagreements and conflicts of instruction might be resolved by those from whom the institutions of doctrine proceed. Nor do we now order anything different from what we ordered before, reversing neither the tenor of our command nor our recollection of the excessive number of those summoned. For when Ambrose, the bishop of the city of Milan, distinguished both by the merit of his life and by God’s favor, suggests that a multitude is unnecessary where truth would not struggle among the many if it were established among the few, and when he suggests that he and the priests of the neighboring cities of Italy would be more than sufficient against the assertions of those who take the opposing side, we have judged that the venerable men should be spared the burden: lest anyone advanced in age, worn down by bodily weakness, or of modest means because of praiseworthy poverty, should have to revisit unfamiliar lands, and so forth.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “See what the Christian emperor has established. He did not wish to wrong the priests; he appointed the bishops themselves as interpreters. Therefore, since we have taken our seats in a council of priests, answer what is put to you. Arius’s letter has been read; it will be read again now, if you wish. From the beginning it contains blasphemies: he said that the Father alone is eternal. If you think that the Son of God is not everlasting, establish this very claim as you wish; if you think it should be condemned, condemn the Gospel. The Apostle is present, and all the Scriptures are available: establish your case from whatever source you wish, if you think that the Son of God is not everlasting.”

Palladius said: “It was done through your efforts, as the reading of the sacred document presented by you indicates, so that there would not be a general and full council. In the absence of our fellow priests [Col. 0434D] we cannot answer.” 487

Bishop Ambrose said: “Who are your associates?”

Palladius said: “The Eastern bishops.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “In earlier times, the council was arranged in such a way that the Easterners, established in the regions of the East, held a council in the East; the Westerners in the West. We, established in the regions of the West, have assembled at the city of Aquileia in accordance with the emperor’s command. Indeed, the prefect of Italy also sent letters saying that, if they wished to assemble, they were at liberty to do so. But because they knew the custom to be that the Easterners should have their council in the East and the Westerners theirs in the West, they therefore thought they should not come.”

Palladius said: “Our emperor Gratian ordered the Easterners to come. Do you deny that he ordered it? The emperor himself told us that he had ordered the Easterners to come.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Certainly he ordered it, since he did not forbid them to come here.”

Palladius said: “But your petition caused them not to come. Under the appearance of a false intention you obtained this and delayed the council.”

[Col. 0435B] Bishop Ambrose said: “There is no need to wander any longer; answer now. Did Arius rightly say that the Father alone is eternal? Did he say this according to the Scriptures, or not?”

Palladius said: “I do not answer you.”

Bishop Constantius said: “You do not answer, after blaspheming for so long?”

Bishop Eusebius said: “But you ought simply to reveal the freedom of your faith. If a pagan demanded of you how you believed in Christ, you ought not to be ashamed to confess.”

Bishop Sabinus said: “You asked that we answer today at your wish, and at your urging we assembled, without waiting for the remaining brothers who could have come. Therefore, you are not free to wander. Do you say that Christ was created, or do you say that the Son of God is everlasting?” [Col. 0435C]

Palladius said: “Did I say this to you? We therefore wrote to you that we would come and prove that you had not acted rightly in deceiving the emperor.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Let Palladius’s letter be read, whether he gave us this instruction; and it will be shown that even now he is deceiving us.”

Palladius said: “Let it certainly be read.”

The bishops said: “When the emperor was present at Sirmium, you appealed to him. Did he himself compel you?” And he added: “What do you answer to this?”

Palladius said: “He said to me, ‘Go.’ We said, ‘Have the Easterners been summoned?’ He replied, ‘They have been summoned.’ If the Easterners had not been summoned, would we have assembled?”

[Col. 0435D] Bishop Ambrose said: “Let the case of the Easterners be set aside; today I seek your own judgment. Arius’s letter has been read to you. You usually deny that you are an Arian. Either condemn Arius today or defend him.”

Palladius said: “It is not within your authority to ask this of me.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “We do not believe that the religious emperor said anything other than what he wrote. He ordered the bishops to assemble; he could not, contrary to his own rescript, have told you alone that the case should not be presented without the Easterners.”

Palladius said: “Were only the Italians ordered to assemble?”

The presbyter and legate Evagrius said: “You promised four days ago, and again two days ago, that you would be present. What, then, were you waiting for? If, as you say, the judgment of your Eastern associates must be awaited, you ought to have given that instruction, not promised a contest.”

Palladius said: “Because I had come as though to a full council, I saw that my associates had not assembled. I came in order to say that you had acted, according to the command, to the prejudice of a future council.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “You yourself demanded that we take our seats today. Indeed, today you yourself said: ‘We Christians have come to Christians.’ You proved that we are Christians. You promised that you would engage in the contest; you promised that you would offer an account. We therefore gladly accepted your opening statement. We wished you to come as a Christian. I presented to you the letter of Arius, written by Arius, whose name, you say, frequently causes you injury. You say that you do not follow Arius. Today your position must be openly stated. Either condemn him or establish your case by whatever readings you wish.” And he added: “Therefore, according to Arius’s letter, is Christ, the Son of God, not everlasting?”

Palladius said: “We said that we would prove ourselves Christians, but in a full council. We do not answer you at all, lest this prejudice the future council.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Without trickery, you must set forth the profession of your faith.” 489

Palladius said: “And what are we reserving for the council?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Condemnation has been pronounced with every voice against the one who denies that the Son of God is everlasting. Arius denied it; Palladius follows him, since he does not wish to condemn Arius. Therefore, consider whether this man’s position is to be approved, and whether he speaks according to the Scriptures or against the Scriptures; it is evident what the answer is. For it has been read: ‘The eternal power and divinity of God.’ Christ is the power of God. Therefore, if God’s power is eternal, Christ is certainly eternal, because Christ is God’s power.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “This is our faith; this is the Catholic understanding. Let anyone who does not say this be anathema.”

All the bishops said: “Anathema.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Does he specifically say that the Father alone is eternal and that the Son began at some time?”

Palladius said: “I have neither seen Arius nor do I know who he is.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Arius’s blasphemy has been brought forward, in which he denies that the Son of God is everlasting. Do you condemn this perfidy together with its author, or do you uphold it?”

Palladius said: “Where the authority of a full council is absent, I do not speak.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Do you hesitate to condemn it after the divine judgments, when he has slipped away from the midst?” And he added: “Let the holy men, the legates of Gaul, speak.”

Bishop Constantius, legate of Gaul, said: “We have always condemned this impiety of that man, and we condemn it now—not only Arius, but anyone who does not call the Son of God everlasting.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “What does my lord Justus also say?”

Bishop Justus, legate of Gaul, said: “Let anyone who does not confess the Son of God coeternal with the Father be held anathema.”

All the bishops said: “Anathema.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Let the legates of Africa also speak, who have brought here the judgments of all their cities.”

Bishop Felix, the legate, said: “If anyone denies that the Son of God is everlasting and denies that he is coeternal, it is not I alone, as legate of the entire province of Africa, who condemn him; the whole priestly chorus that sent me to this most holy assembly also condemned him beforehand.”

Bishop Anemius said: “The capital of Illyricum is none other than the city of Sirmium. I, therefore, am the bishop of that city. I pronounce anathema upon him who does not confess the Son of God to be eternal and coeternal with the Father, which means everlasting; and also upon those who do not confess the same.” 490

Bishop Ambrose said: “Hear what follows.” And it was read: “‘The only eternal one, the only one without beginning, the only true one, the only one possessing immortality.’”

Bishop Ambrose said: “And in this condemn him who denies that the Son is true God. For since he himself is truth, how is he not true God?” And he added: “What do you say to this?”

Palladius said: “Who does not call the Son true?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Arius denied it.”

Palladius said: “Since the Apostle says that Christ is God over all, can anyone deny the true Son of God?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “So that you may know how simply we seek the truth, behold, I say what you say, but I regard it as incomplete. For when you say it in this way, you appear to deny true God; but if you simply confess the Son of God as true God, establish it in the order that I myself propose.”

Palladius said: “I speak to you according to the Scriptures; I call the true Son of God ‘Lord.’”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Do you call the Son of God the true Lord?”

Palladius said: “When I call him the true Son, what more is required?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “I do not ask merely that you call him the true Son, but that you call the true Lord the Son of God.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Is Christ true God, according to the faith of all and the Catholic confession?”

[Col. 0437D] Palladius said: “He is the true Son of God.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “For we too are sons by adoption, whereas he is so according to the proper nature of divine generation.” And he added: “Do you therefore confess that the true Son of God is the true Lord, according to divinity and proper nature?”

Palladius said: “I call him the true, only-begotten Son of God.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Do you therefore think it contrary to the Scriptures if Christ is called true God?”

When Palladius remained silent, Bishop Ambrose said: “The one who calls him only the true Son of God and does not wish to call him the true Lord appears to deny him. Let Palladius therefore confess in this order—if indeed he confesses—and say whether he calls the Son of God ‘Lord.’” 491

Palladius said: “When the Son says, ‘That they may know you, the only true Lord, and Jesus Christ whom you sent’ (John 17:3), is this said with affection or with truth?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “John said in his Epistle: ‘This is the true God’ (1 John 5:20). Deny this.”

Palladius said: “When I call him the true Son, I also profess true divinity.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “And here lies the deception. For you are accustomed to speak of one and true divinity in such a way that you call only the Father’s divinity true and one, not the Son’s as well. Therefore, if you wish to speak openly—since you appeal to the Scriptures—say what the evangelist John said: ‘This is the true God,’ or deny that it was said.”

Palladius said: “Apart from the Son, there is no other one begotten.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Is Christ true God according to the faith of all and the Catholic confession, or, according to your position, is he not true God?”

Palladius said: “He is the power of our God.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “You do not have the freedom to profess it; therefore, anathema to him who does not confess the Son of God as true God.”

All the bishops said: “Let him be anathema who does not call Christ, the Son of God, the true Lord.” He added again: “‘The only true one, the only one possessing immortality.’”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Does the Son of God possess immortality, or does he not possess it, according to his divinity?”

[Col. 0438C] Palladius said: “Do you accept the Apostle, or not? ‘The King of kings, who alone possesses immortality’ (1 Tim. 6:16).”

Bishop Ambrose said: “What do you say about Christ, the Son of God?”

Palladius said: “Is ‘Christ’ a divine name or a human name?”

Bishop Eusebius said: “According to the mystery of the flesh he is called Christ; but he is the same one, God and man.”

Palladius said: “Christ is a name of the flesh; Christ is a human name. And you answer me.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Why do you linger over irrelevant matters? When Arius’s impiety was being read—his claim that the Father alone possesses immortality—you brought forward, in agreement with Arius’s impiety, the testimony from the Apostle: ‘Who alone possesses immortality and dwells in inaccessible light’ (ibid.). But if you understand it, he expressed the dignity of the whole nature under the name of God, since under the name of God the Father and the Son are designated.” 492

Palladius said: “And you refused to answer what I asked you.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “I ask your position openly: does the Son of God possess immortality according to divine generation, or does he not possess it?”

Palladius said: “According to divine generation he is incorruptible; through the flesh he died.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “It was not divinity that died, but the flesh died.”

Palladius said: “Answer me first.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Does the Son of God possess immortality according to divinity, or does he not? But you have also revealed your deceptions and snares, not according to Arius’s profession.” And he added: “What is your judgment of the one who denies that the Son of God possesses immortality?”

All the bishops said: “Let him be anathema.”

Palladius said: “Is the divine status immortal?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “This too is cunning, so that you express nothing clearly about the Son of God. I say that the Son of God possesses immortality according to divinity. Either deny that he is ‘the one who possesses immortality.’”

Palladius said: “Did Christ die, or did he not?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “According to the flesh. Our soul does not die. For it is written: ‘Do not fear those who can kill the flesh but cannot kill the soul’ (Matt. 10:28). Since, then, our soul cannot die, do you think that Christ died according to divinity?”

Palladius said: “Why do you shrink from the designation of death?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “On the contrary, I do not shrink from it, but I confess it according to my flesh. For there is one through whom I have been released from the bonds of death.”

Palladius said: “Death is caused by the separation of the spirit. For Christ the Son of God assumed flesh, and through the flesh he died.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “It is written that Christ suffered. Therefore, he suffered according to the flesh; according to divinity he possesses immortality. Whoever denies this is the devil.”

Palladius said: “I do not know Arius.”

[Col. 0439C] Bishop Ambrose said: “Then Arius was wrong, since the Son of God too possesses immortality according to divinity.” And he added: “Was he right or wrong?”

Palladius said: “I do not agree.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “With whom do you not agree? Anathema to him who does not openly state the freedom of his faith.”

All the bishops said: “Anathema.”

Palladius said: “Say what you wish; the divinity is immortal.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Whose? The Father’s, or the Son’s as well?” And he added: “Arius amassed many impieties; let us proceed to the others.” And it was read: “THE ONLY WISE ONE.”

Palladius said: “The Father is wise from himself, but the Son is not wise.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Then the Son is not wise, although he himself is Wisdom? For we also say that the Son was born from the Father.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Is anything so impious, so profane, as to deny the Son of God wisdom, as he has done?”

Palladius said: “He is called Wisdom. Who could deny Wisdom?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Is he wise, or is he not?”

Palladius said: “He is Wisdom.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Then he is wise, since he is Wisdom.”

Palladius said: “We answer you according to the Scriptures.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “As far as I can see, Palladius has even attempted to deny that the Son of God is wise.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Let him be anathema who denies that the Son of God is wise.”

All the bishops said: “Anathema.”

Eusebius said: “Let Secundianus also answer this.”

When Secundianus remained silent, Bishop Ambrose said: “The one who is silent wishes to retain a judgment free from commitment.” And he added: “When he says that the Father alone is good, did he confess or deny the Son?”

Palladius said: “We read, ‘I am the good shepherd’ (John 10:11), and do we deny this? Who would not call the Son of God good?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Then Christ is good?”

Palladius said: “Good.”

[Col. 0440B] Bishop Ambrose said: “Then Arius was wrong to speak of the Father alone, since the Son of God too is God to all.”

Palladius said: “Whoever does not call Christ good speaks wrongly.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Do you confess Christ as the good God? For I too am good. He said to me, ‘Well done, good servant’ (Matt. 25:21). And: ‘The good man brings forth good things from his treasure’ (Luke 6:45).”

Palladius said: “I have already spoken; now I do not answer you until the full council.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “The Jews said, ‘He is good’; and Arius denies that the Son of God is good.”

Palladius said: “Who could deny this?” 494

Bishop Eusebius said: “Then God, the Son of God, is good.”

[Col. 0440C] Palladius said: “The good Father begot the good Son.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “He also begot us as good, but not according to divinity. Do you call the Son of God the good God?”

Palladius said: “The Son of God is good.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “You see, then, that you call Christ a good Son, but not the good God, which is what is being asked of you.” And he added: “Anathema to him who does not confess the Son of God as the good God.”

All the bishops said: “Anathema.” He then read: “THE ONLY POWERFUL ONE.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Is the Son of God powerful, or is he not?”

Palladius said: “He who made all things—is he not powerful? He who made all things—is he less powerful?”

[Col. 0440D] Bishop Ambrose said: “Then Arius was wrong.” And he added: “Do you condemn Arius in this matter as well?”

Palladius said: “How do I know who knows? I answer you for myself.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Is the Son of the Lord God powerful?”

Palladius said: “Powerful.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Is God good?”

Palladius said: “I have already said that the only-begotten Son of God is powerful.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “The powerful Lord?”

Palladius said: “The powerful Son of God.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Human beings too are powerful. It is written: ‘Why do you boast in wickedness, you who are powerful in iniquity?’ (Ps. 52:3). And elsewhere: ‘When I am weak, then I am powerful’ (2 Cor. 12:10). What I require of you is that you confess the Lord Christ, the Son of God, to be powerful; or, if you deny it, establish your case. For when I say that the Father and the Son have one power, I call the Son of God powerful just as I call the Father powerful. Do you hesitate, then, to confess that the Lord, the Son of God, is powerful?”

Palladius said: “I have already said that, according to the argument, we answer you as best we can. You alone wish to be judges; you wish to be the litigants. We do not answer you now, but we shall answer you in a general and full council.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Anathema to him who denies the Lord Christ as powerful.”

All the bishops said: “Anathema.” Again it was read: “THE ONLY POWERFUL ONE, JUDGE OF ALL.”

Palladius said: “The Son of God is judge of all. There is one who gives, and there is one who receives.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Did he give by grace or by nature? Judgment is also given to human beings.” 495

Palladius said: “Do you say that the Father is greater, or not?”

Bishop Ambrose said: “I shall answer you later.”

Palladius said: “I shall not answer you if you do not answer me.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “Unless you condemn Arius’s impiety in due order, we shall not give you the opportunity to ask questions.”

Palladius said: “I do not answer you.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Is the Son of God, as it has been read, judge or not?”

[Col. 0441C] Palladius said: “If you do not answer me, I do not answer you as an impious man.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “You have my profession, by which I shall answer you. In the meantime, let Arius’s letter be read through. And he added: “In Arius’s letter you will find this sacrilege also, which you are contriving.”

Palladius said: “You do not answer what I ask.”

Bishop Eusebius said: “We call the Son of God equal God.”

Palladius said: “You are the judge; your recorders are here.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Let your own men write, if they wish.”

Palladius said: “Is the Father greater, or not?”

Bishop Eusebius said: “According to divinity, the Son is equal to the Father. You have in the Gospel that the Jews persecuted him because he not only violated the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal to God (John 5:18). What the impious persecutors confessed, we believers cannot deny.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “And elsewhere you have: ‘Although he was in the form of God, he did not regard equality with God as something to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of human beings, obedient unto death’ (Phil. 2:6–8).” And he added: “You see that he is equal in the form of God? ‘And he took,’ he says, ‘the form of a servant.’ In what, then, is he lesser? Certainly according to the form of a servant, not of God.”

[Col. 0442A] Bishop Eusebius said: “Just as, while constituted in the form of a servant, he was not inferior to a servant, so, while constituted in the form of God, he could not be inferior to God.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “Or say that the Son of God is lesser according to divinity.”

Palladius said: “The Father is greater.”

Bishop Ambrose said: “According to the flesh.”

Palladius said: “‘The one who sent me is greater than I.’ Was the flesh sent by God, or the Son of God?” 496
